item.title: PM Rabuka meets Health Workers after dramatic sea rescue
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 02/08/2026 Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka took time this afternoon to visit the six health professionals who were lost at sea in Lau for more than 30 hours.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 02/08/2026

Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka took time this afternoon to visit the six health professionals who were lost at sea in Lau for more than 30 hours.

The six are receiving medical treatment at Twomey Hospital in Tamavua after being flown from Lakeba to Suva on Friday.

According to the Ministry of Health, the team departed Moce Island at 7am on Wednesday bound for Oneata and was expected to arrive about two hours later.

After they failed to arrive as scheduled, the district nurse in Oneata contacted the Lakeba Sub-Divisional Hospital, prompting search and rescue efforts.

The Ministry says the boat handler was found on Thursday morning and told rescuers that after the engine failed, the vessel began taking on water.

The medical team removed the wooden floorboards from the boat to use as flotation devices while wearing their life jackets.

In an effort to get mobile phone reception, the boat handler swam towards Aiwa Island, leaving the rest of the medical team together and safe in the water.

The six healthcare workers were eventually rescued on Thursday night by the captain and crew of Lomaiviti Princess 12.

item.content:encoded:
A formal investigation has been initiated to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident at t he Fiji Corrections Service as they are aware of the incident circulating on social media involving an alleged assault at the Lautoka Remand Centre.

In a statement, the Fiji Corrections Service says violence or assault of any kind, whether committed by an officer against a prisoner or by a prisoner against an officer, is not tolerated.

The Service says any individual found to have abused their authority or engaged in unlawful conduct will be held accountable in accordance with the law.

The Fiji Corrections Service has assured the public that a comprehensive update will be provided once the investigation is complete.

item.title: Style Fiji 2026 to turn glamour into action for HIV awareness
item.description: Style Fiji 2026 will support HIV Fiji as one of its charity partners this year, with organisers hoping to use the country's premier fashion event to help raise awareness and funds for one of Fiji's most pressing public health challenges. item.content:encoded:
Style Fiji 2026 will support HIV Fiji as one of its charity partners this year, with organisers hoping to use the country's premier fashion event to help raise awareness and funds for one of Fiji's most pressing public health challenges.

Speaking at the launch of Style Fiji 2026 last night , Style Fiji committee member and Creative Director, Samson Lee, said while fashion is what brings people together, the event has always been driven by a greater purpose.

Lee says Fiji is facing one of the most significant public health challenges in its history, with HIV cases rising sharply in recent years.

He says behind every statistic is a person, a family and a future, and far too many people continue to live with stigma, fear and misunderstanding.

Lee says through Style Fiji, they hope to shine a light on the cause by supporting HIV Fiji in its work to assist people living with and affected by HIV, educate communities and advocate for a healthier Fiji.

He says the event aims to replace fear with understanding and stigma with hope through fashion, generosity and unity.

Lee also announced that the Fiji Mobility Alliance, formerly the Spinal Injury Association of Fiji, will again benefit from this year's event after Style Fiji raised $50,000 for the organisation during last year's show.

He says the funds are already making a meaningful difference, with the alliance expecting a shipment of assistive devices later this year to support people with disabilities across Fiji.

Meanwhile, Style Fiji 2026 will be held on 7th November at the Sheraton Fiji Golf & Beach Resort under the theme "A Midsummer Night's Dream," inspired by William Shakespeare's classic play.

A new addition this year will be the Style Fiji Market, which will be held on the morning of the fashion show and showcase local designers, artisans, makers and small businesses.

Lee says organisers hope the market will become an annual tradition celebrating Fijian creativity while encouraging people to support local businesses.

Tickets for Style Fiji 2026 is officially on sale following last night's launch.

item.title: Communities must work with Government to fight drugs - Naivalurua
item.description: Minister for Policing and Communication Ioane Naivalurua is calling on communities in the Northern Division to work together with Government in the fight against drugs. While closing the Duavata Northern Crime Prevention Carnival in Labasa last night, Naivalurua stressed that the eradication of crime and drugs is possible if communities work together.
item.content:encoded:
Minister for Policing and Communication Ioane Naivalurua is calling on communities in the Northern Division to work together with Government in the fight against drugs.

While closing the Duavata Northern Crime Prevention Carnival in Labasa last night, Naivalurua stressed that the eradication of crime and drugs is possible if communities work together.

He is calling on people to come forward and be part of the effort to address crime and drug-related issues, saying communities should not remain on the sidelines by simply gossiping and commenting.

He says Government is committed to the fight and is urging people to come to the frontline where the battle is being fought.

The Minister says that during the one-week carnival, contestants raised these issues, and the Police remain committed to addressing them.

He says that, as the Minister responsible for Policing, combating crime and drugs would be a difficult task without the support of communities.

He says that, with the new financial year underway, the Fiji Police Force will continue its fight with its new budget allocation, along with new laws that are being introduced.

Naivalurua says the new Police Bill will help Police combat crime, while the Government's decision to establish a new Counter Narcotics Bureau will focus on combating drugs.

He is calling on everyone to work together in the spirit of Duavata to maintain a stable, peaceful and resilient Fiji.
